items.title: Glover Compton Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: Big plays where all the big stars like Mr. Bowler, Alderman of the Northside, Alderman of the 43rd of Watt, Patty Bowler, and the Mayor Cermak that got killed out there. Oh, yes. Yeah, they used to come to the Royal Box, all that, that class of people.

ctx.x: You want to go, or should I go? There. Okay, it's going again.

See, my entertainers in the past were all the old-time well-known American white entertainers. Roy, Roy was a, he and I alternated at the piano. Roy Barton. Roy Barton. Oh, yeah. Chicago boy, Irish boy. And Paul Farrell. And Bill Hanley. That was my entertainers at the Irish New York bar five years. And then at the Royal Box, so we could Cricket Smith. There are two bands out of the Royal Addison. Big plays where all the big stars like Mr. Bowler, Alderman of the Northside, Alderman of the 43rd of Watt, Patty…
In the old days here in Chicago, were there many gang fights around when you were playing here in the Prohibition? No, no. Has Al Capone taken over yet or not? No, no. I never, never saw a fight.
